Ch 11 · Areas Related to Circles — Practice

Attempt first, then open the answer. Everything here is original practice material mapped to the current syllabus.

MCQs

The area of a quadrant of a circle of radius r is: (a) πr²/2 (b) πr²/4 (c) 2πr (d) πr²

(b) πr²/4.

The perimeter of a sector includes: (a) only the arc (b) the arc and one radius (c) the arc and two radii (d) the chord and the arc

(c) The arc and two radii.

The area of a segment is found by: (a) sector − triangle (b) sector + triangle (c) circle − sector (d) triangle − sector

(a) Sector − triangle.

Written questions

2 marks Find the length of an arc of a sector with radius 21 cm and central angle 120°.

Arc = (120/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 21 = (1/3) × 132 = 44 cm.

3 marks Find the area of a sector of radius 6 cm with a central angle of 60° (take π = 3.14).

Area = (60/360) × 3.14 × 36 = (1/6) × 113.04 = 18.84 cm².

3 marks Find the perimeter of a sector with radius 14 cm and central angle 90°.

Arc = (90/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 14 = (1/4) × 88 = 22 cm.
Perimeter = 2(14) + 22 = 50 cm.

4 marks A square of side 14 cm has a circle inscribed in it. Find the area between the square and the circle.

The inscribed circle has diameter 14 cm, so radius 7 cm.
Area of square = 196 cm². Area of circle = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm².
Required area = 196 − 154 = 42 cm².
